responses_by_run.answer: Athena turned Arachne into a spider as punishment for her pride and defiance [1]. Arachne was an exceptionally skilled weaver who refused to acknowledge that her talent came from Athena, instead claiming her knowledge was entirely her own [1]. When Athena challenged her to a weaving contest in disguise, Arachne arrogantly refused to show respect and demanded the goddess come herself [1]. After Athena revealed her true identity and the two competed, Athena found Arachne's work flawless but was enraged by her skill and defiance [2]. Athena destroyed Arachne's web and struck her repeatedly [2]. When Arachne attempted to hang herself in despair, Athena saved her life but pronounced a cruel eternal punishment: she transformed Arachne into a spider, condemning her to dangle on a cord forever and to weave endlessly as a spider, so that her punishment would last throughout all generations [3].

Prometheus was punished for two main transgressions: stealing fire and giving it to humans [1][2][3], and for attempting to deceive Zeus during a dispute at Mecone by dividing sacrificial portions unfairly [2][3]. When Zeus discovered that Prometheus had hidden fire in a stalk of fennel and given it to mortals, he ordered Hephaestus to bind Prometheus to Mount Caucasus with inextricable bonds and set an eagle upon him to devour his liver daily [1]—a torment that lasted many years until Heracles eventually freed him [1].

Odysseus escaped Polyphemus through a two-part plan. First, he blinded the Cyclops by sharpening a wooden club, heating it in fire, and driving it into Polyphemus's eye with the help of his comrades [1][2]. When Polyphemus cried out for help from other Cyclopes, they left him alone after he said "Nobody" was hurting him, misunderstanding his words [1][2]. Second, after the blinding, Odysseus tied the sheep together in groups of three and hid himself under the largest ram, clinging to its fleece [3][4]. When Polyphemus opened the cave to let his flocks out to pasture, he felt the sheep as they passed but could not detect the men hidden beneath them [3][4]. Odysseus and his comrades thus escaped with the sheep to their ships [3][4].
